1	# eShop Reference Application - "AdventureWorks"
2	
3	A reference .NET application implementing an e-commerce website using a services-based architecture using [.NET Aspire](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspire/).
4	
5	![eShop Reference Application architecture diagram](img/eshop_architecture.png)
6	
7	![eShop homepage screenshot](img/eshop_homepage.png)
8	
9	## Getting Started
10	
11	This version of eShop is based on .NET 9. 
12	
13	Previous eShop versions:
14	* [.NET 8](https://github.com/dotnet/eShop/tree/release/8.0)
15	
16	### Prerequisites
17	
18	- Clone the eShop repository: https://github.com/dotnet/eshop
19	- [Install & start Docker Desktop](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/)
20	
21	#### Windows with Visual Studio
22	- Install [Visual Studio 2022 version 17.10 or newer](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/).
23	  - Select the following workloads:
24	    - `ASP.NET and web development` workload.
25	    - `.NET Aspire SDK` component in `Individual components`.
26	    - Optional: `.NET Multi-platform App UI development` to run client apps
27	
28	Or
29	
30	- Run the following commands in a Powershell & Terminal running as `Administrator` to automatically configure your environment with the required tools to build and run this application. (Note: A restart is required and included in the script below.)
31	
32	```powershell
33	install-Module -Name Microsoft.WinGet.Configuration -AllowPrerelease -AcceptLicense -Force
34	$env:Path = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine") + ";" + [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","User")
35	get-WinGetConfiguration -file .\.configurations\vside.dsc.yaml | Invoke-WinGetConfiguration -AcceptConfigurationAgreements
36	```
37	
38	Or
39	
40	- From Dev Home go to `Machine Configuration -> Clone repositories`. Enter the URL for this repository. In the confirmation screen look for the section `Configuration File Detected` and click `Run File`.
41	
42	#### Mac, Linux, & Windows without Visual Studio
43	- Install the latest [.NET 9 SDK](https://dot.net/download?cid=eshop)
44	
45	Or
46	
47	- Run the following commands in a Powershell & Terminal running as `Administrator` to automatically configuration your environment with the required tools to build and run this application. (Note: A restart is required after running the script below.)
48	
49	##### Install Visual Studio Code and related extensions
50	```powershell
51	install-Module -Name Microsoft.WinGet.Configuration -AllowPrerelease -AcceptLicense  -Force
52	$env:Path = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine") + ";" + [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","User")
53	get-WinGetConfiguration -file .\.configurations\vscode.dsc.yaml | Invoke-WinGetConfiguration -AcceptConfigurationAgreements
54	```
55	
56	> Note: These commands may require `sudo`
57	
58	- Optional: Install [Visual Studio Code with C# Dev Kit](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/csharp/get-started)
59	- Optional: Install [.NET MAUI Workload](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/maui/get-started/installation?tabs=visual-studio-code)
60	
61	> Note: When running on Mac with Apple Silicon (M series processor), Rosetta 2 for grpc-tools. 
62	
63	### Running the solution
64	
65	> [!WARNING]
66	> Remember to ensure that Docker is started
67	
68	* (Windows only) Run the application from Visual Studio:
69	 - Open the `eShop.Web.slnf` file in Visual Studio
70	 - Ensure that `eShop.AppHost.csproj` is your startup project
71	 - Hit Ctrl-F5 to launch Aspire
72	
73	* Or run the application from your terminal:
74	```powershell
75	dotnet run --project src/eShop.AppHost/eShop.AppHost.csproj
76	```
77	then look for lines like this in the console output in order to find the URL to open the Aspire dashboard:
78	```sh
79	Login to the dashboard at: http://localhost:19888/login?t=uniquelogincodeforyou
80	```
81	
82	> You may need to install ASP.NET Core HTTPS development certificates first, and then close all browser tabs. Learn more at https://aka.ms/aspnet/https-trust-dev-cert
83	
84	### Azure Open AI
85	
86	When using Azure OpenAI, inside *eShop.AppHost/appsettings.json*, add the following section:
87	
88	```json
89	  "ConnectionStrings": {
90	    "OpenAi": "Endpoint=xxx;Key=xxx;"
91	  }
92	```
93	
94	Replace the values with your own. Then, in the eShop.AppHost *Program.cs*, set this value to **true**
95	
96	```csharp
97	bool useOpenAI = false;
98	```
99	
100	Here's additional guidance on the [.NET Aspire OpenAI component](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspire/azureai/azureai-openai-component?tabs=dotnet-cli). 
101	
102	### Use Azure Developer CLI
103	
104	You can use the [Azure Developer CLI](https://aka.ms/azd) to run this project on Azure with only a few commands. Follow the next instructions:
105	
106	- Install the latest or update to the latest [Azure Developer CLI (azd)](https://aka.ms/azure-dev/install).
107	- Log in `azd` (if you haven't done it before) to your Azure account:
108	```sh
109	azd auth login
110	```
111	- Initialize `azd` from the root of the repo.
112	```sh
113	azd init
114	```
115	- During init:
116	  - Select `Use code in the current directory`. Azd will automatically detect the .NET Aspire project.
117	  - Confirm `.NET (Aspire)` and continue.
118	  - Select which services to expose to the Internet (exposing `webapp` is enough to test the sample).
119	  - Finalize the initialization by giving a name to your environment.
120	
121	- Create Azure resources and deploy the sample by running:
122	```sh
123	azd up
124	```
125	Notes:
126	  - The operation takes a few minutes the first time it is ever run for an environment.
127	  - At the end of the process, `azd` will display the `url` for the webapp. Follow that link to test the sample.
128	  - You can run `azd up` after saving changes to the sample to re-deploy and update the sample.
129	  - Report any issues to [azure-dev](https://github.com/Azure/azure-dev/issues) repo.
130	  - [FAQ and troubleshoot](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/developer/azure-developer-cli/troubleshoot?tabs=Browser) for azd.
131	
132	## Contributing
133	
134	For more information on contributing to this repo, read [the contribution documentation](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and [the Code of Conduct](CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
135	
136	### Sample data
137	
138	The sample catalog data is defined in [catalog.json](https://github.com/dotnet/eShop/blob/main/src/Catalog.API/Setup/catalog.json). Those product names, descriptions, and brand names are fictional and were generated using [GPT-35-Turbo](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/how-to/chatgpt), and the corresponding [product images](https://github.com/dotnet/eShop/tree/main/src/Catalog.API/Pics) were generated using [DALL·E 3](https://openai.com/dall-e-3).
139	
140	## eShop on Azure
141	
142	For a version of this app configured for deployment on Azure, please view [the eShop on Azure](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/eShopOnAzure) repo.
143

# eShop Reference Application - "AdventureWorks"

A reference .NET application implementing an e-commerce website using a services-based architecture using [.NET Aspire](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspire/).

![eShop Reference Application architecture diagram](img/eshop_architecture.png)

![eShop homepage screenshot](img/eshop_homepage.png)

## Getting Started

This version of eShop is based on .NET 9. 

Previous eShop versions:
* [.NET 8](https://github.com/dotnet/eShop/tree/release/8.0)

### Prerequisites

- Clone the eShop repository: https://github.com/dotnet/eshop
- [Install & start Docker Desktop](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/)

#### Windows with Visual Studio
- Install [Visual Studio 2022 version 17.10 or newer](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/).
  - Select the following workloads:
    - `ASP.NET and web development` workload.
    - `.NET Aspire SDK` component in `Individual components`.
    - Optional: `.NET Multi-platform App UI development` to run client apps

Or

- Run the following commands in a Powershell & Terminal running as `Administrator` to automatically configure your environment with the required tools to build and run this application. (Note: A restart is required and included in the script below.)

```powershell
install-Module -Name Microsoft.WinGet.Configuration -AllowPrerelease -AcceptLicense -Force
$env:Path = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine") + ";" + [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","User")
get-WinGetConfiguration -file .\.configurations\vside.dsc.yaml | Invoke-WinGetConfiguration -AcceptConfigurationAgreements
```

Or

- From Dev Home go to `Machine Configuration -> Clone repositories`. Enter the URL for this repository. In the confirmation screen look for the section `Configuration File Detected` and click `Run File`.

#### Mac, Linux, & Windows without Visual Studio
- Install the latest [.NET 9 SDK](https://dot.net/download?cid=eshop)

Or

- Run the following commands in a Powershell & Terminal running as `Administrator` to automatically configuration your environment with the required tools to build and run this application. (Note: A restart is required after running the script below.)

##### Install Visual Studio Code and related extensions
```powershell
install-Module -Name Microsoft.WinGet.Configuration -AllowPrerelease -AcceptLicense  -Force
$env:Path = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine") + ";" + [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","User")
get-WinGetConfiguration -file .\.configurations\vscode.dsc.yaml | Invoke-WinGetConfiguration -AcceptConfigurationAgreements
```

> Note: These commands may require `sudo`

- Optional: Install [Visual Studio Code with C# Dev Kit](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/csharp/get-started)
- Optional: Install [.NET MAUI Workload](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/maui/get-started/installation?tabs=visual-studio-code)

> Note: When running on Mac with Apple Silicon (M series processor), Rosetta 2 for grpc-tools. 

### Running the solution

> [!WARNING]
> Remember to ensure that Docker is started

* (Windows only) Run the application from Visual Studio:
 - Open the `eShop.Web.slnf` file in Visual Studio
 - Ensure that `eShop.AppHost.csproj` is your startup project
 - Hit Ctrl-F5 to launch Aspire

* Or run the application from your terminal:
```powershell
dotnet run --project src/eShop.AppHost/eShop.AppHost.csproj
```
then look for lines like this in the console output in order to find the URL to open the Aspire dashboard:
```sh
Login to the dashboard at: http://localhost:19888/login?t=uniquelogincodeforyou
```

> You may need to install ASP.NET Core HTTPS development certificates first, and then close all browser tabs. Learn more at https://aka.ms/aspnet/https-trust-dev-cert

### Azure Open AI

When using Azure OpenAI, inside *eShop.AppHost/appsettings.json*, add the following section:

```json
  "ConnectionStrings": {
    "OpenAi": "Endpoint=xxx;Key=xxx;"
  }
```

Replace the values with your own. Then, in the eShop.AppHost *Program.cs*, set this value to **true**

```csharp
bool useOpenAI = false;
```

Here's additional guidance on the [.NET Aspire OpenAI component](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspire/azureai/azureai-openai-component?tabs=dotnet-cli). 

### Use Azure Developer CLI

You can use the [Azure Developer CLI](https://aka.ms/azd) to run this project on Azure with only a few commands. Follow the next instructions:

- Install the latest or update to the latest [Azure Developer CLI (azd)](https://aka.ms/azure-dev/install).
- Log in `azd` (if you haven't done it before) to your Azure account:
```sh
azd auth login
```
- Initialize `azd` from the root of the repo.
```sh
azd init
```
- During init:
  - Select `Use code in the current directory`. Azd will automatically detect the .NET Aspire project.
  - Confirm `.NET (Aspire)` and continue.
  - Select which services to expose to the Internet (exposing `webapp` is enough to test the sample).
  - Finalize the initialization by giving a name to your environment.

- Create Azure resources and deploy the sample by running:
```sh
azd up
```
Notes:
  - The operation takes a few minutes the first time it is ever run for an environment.
  - At the end of the process, `azd` will display the `url` for the webapp. Follow that link to test the sample.
  - You can run `azd up` after saving changes to the sample to re-deploy and update the sample.

content.text:
I have everything I need.

## What kind of system this is

**eShop is a .NET Aspire–orchestrated, microservices-based e-commerce reference application** ("AdventureWorks") — a distributed set of ASP.NET Core services, background workers, a Blazor Server storefront, and two .NET MAUI mobile clients, wired together by an Aspire AppHost that also provisions Redis, RabbitMQ, and PostgreSQL containers (`README.md:1-3`, `eShop.slnx:1-36`).

Communication is mixed: HTTP/REST between web and APIs, gRPC to the basket service, and RabbitMQ integration events between services (`src/Basket.API/Program.cs:6,12`, `src/PaymentProcessor/Program.cs:5-6`).

## The single runnable entry point

**`src/eShop.AppHost`** is the one thing you run. It is an Aspire AppHost (`<Project Sdk="Aspire.AppHost.Sdk/13.2.0">`, `OutputType=Exe`) whose `Program.cs` *is* the composition root: `DistributedApplication.CreateBuilder(args)` … `builder.Build().Run()` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:3,103`). Launch it with `dotnet run --project src/eShop.AppHost/eShop.AppHost.csproj`, or open `eShop.Web.slnf` in Visual Studio with `eShop.AppHost.csproj` as startup (`README.md:68-76`). The Aspire dashboard listens on `https://localhost:19888` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Properties/launchSettings.json`).

## Processes that start when the solution runs

Each of these is added by an `AddProject<...>` call in the AppHost:

| Resource name | Project | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `identity-api` | Identity.API | ASP.NET Core web API / IdentityServer, externally exposed, `/health` check (`Program.cs:23-26`) |
| `basket-api` | Basket.API | gRPC service (`Program.cs:30`; `src/Basket.API/Program.cs:6,12`) |
| `catalog-api` | Catalog.API | ASP.NET Core web API (`Program.cs:36-38`) |
| `ordering-api` | Ordering.API | ASP.NET Core web API, owns the EF migrations (`Program.cs:40-44,49`) |
| `order-processor` | OrderProcessor | Worker SDK host running the `GracePeriodManagerService` hosted service (`Program.cs:46-49`; `src/OrderProcessor/Extensions/Extensions.cs:19`) |
| `payment-processor` | PaymentProcessor | Event-bus subscriber for `OrderStatusChangedToStockConfirmedIntegrationEvent` (`Program.cs:51-52`; `src/PaymentProcessor/Program.cs:5-6`) |
| `webhooks-api` | Webhooks.API | ASP.NET Core web API (`Program.cs:54-57`) |
| `mobile-bff` | — (YARP resource) | Reverse proxy / BFF routing to catalog, ordering, identity (`Program.cs:60-62`; routes in `src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:185-249`) |
| `webhooksclient` | WebhookClient | Web UI demo client (`Program.cs:65-67`) |
| `webapp` | WebApp | The storefront — Blazor with interactive server render mode (`Program.cs:69-77`; `src/WebApp/Program.cs:8,30`) |

Plus three container resources: `redis`, `eventbus` (RabbitMQ, persistent lifetime), and `postgres` (image `ankane/pgvector`, persistent) hosting four databases — `catalogdb`, `identitydb`, `orderingdb`, `webhooksdb` (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:7-18`).

## What composes them

`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs` alone. It:
- Declares infrastructure, then wires each service with `.WithReference(...)` / `.WaitFor(...)` for connection strings and startup ordering (`Program.cs:30-57`).
- Injects cross-service URLs as environment variables — `Identity__Url` into basket/ordering/webhooks, `IdentityUrl` into the UIs, and a cyclic set of callback URLs back into identity-api (`Program.cs:33,44,57,67,77,97-101`).
- Picks the `http` vs `https` launch profile from the `ESHOP_USE_HTTP_ENDPOINTS` env var (`Program.cs:20,108-115`).
- Has two opt-in AI paths, **both hard-coded off**: `useOpenAI` and `useOllama` are `false`, so no OpenAI or Ollama resource starts by default (`Program.cs:80-90`; helpers at `src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:52,164`).

`src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:22-47` also forces `ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED=true` onto every project resource via a `BeforeStartEvent` hook.

## Not started by the AppHost

Two runnable apps exist in `eShop.slnx` but are **not** referenced by the AppHost and must be launched separately from a device/emulator target:
- **`src/ClientApp`** — .NET MAUI native app, entry `MauiProgram.CreateMauiApp()` (`src/ClientApp/MauiProgram.cs:23-27`), multi-targeting android/ios/maccatalyst/windows.
- **`src/HybridApp`** — MAUI Blazor Hybrid app reusing `WebAppComponents`, entry `MauiProgram.CreateMauiApp()` (`src/HybridApp/MauiProgram.cs:12-34`). It talks to the `mobile-bff` YARP proxy at a hard-coded `localhost:11632` (`src/HybridApp/MauiProgram.cs:9`), so the AppHost must already be running.

The remaining projects are libraries, not processes: `eShop.ServiceDefaults`, `EventBus`, `EventBusRabbitMQ`, `IntegrationEventLogEF`, `Ordering.Domain`, `Ordering.Infrastructure`, `WebAppComponents` (`eShop.slnx:6-19`).

One caveat: I confirmed the MAUI apps are absent from the AppHost by reading `Program.cs` end to end — there is no `Projects.ClientApp` or `Projects.HybridApp` reference in it — but I did not check whether some external tooling (e.g. `azd`) launches them another way.
